mnemonic: It is composed of two kanji: 仕 (serve/do) and 事 (thing/matter). Think of it as 'a matter of things you do'. Don't confuse 仕事 (shigoto) with 働く (hataraku), which is the verb 'to work'.
examples: - 今日は仕事があります。 = I have work today.
- 父は毎日仕事に行きます。 = My father goes to work every day.
- 私の仕事は日本語を教えることです。 = My job is teaching Japanese.
- 仕事が終わりました。 = Work is finished.

mnemonic: Remember: the opposite of 後 is 前 (まえ), 'before' or 'in front'
examples: Be careful! 後 has different pronunciations depending on its meaning and context. あと means 'after' or 'later' in kanji, and 'what remains' in hiragana. 後ろ (うしろ) means 'behind' or 'the back'.
It can also be read ご in compound words, such as: 食後 (しょくご) meaning 'after a meal'.
- 後で電話します。 = I'll call you later.
- 仕事の後で友達に会います。 = I'll meet my friend after work.
- 後ろに人がいます。 = There is a person behind me.
- あと一つあります。 = There is one more.

mnemonic: It is composed of 過 (exceed/pass) and す (the hiragana ending). You can find it in expressions such as 過ごし方 (すごしかた), meaning 'way of spending time'.
examples: 過ぎる (すぎる) means 'to pass' or 'to exceed', while 過ごす focuses on spending or passing time.
- 週末は家で過ごします。 = I spend the weekend at home.
- 友達と楽しく過ごしました。 = I had a good time with my friends.
- 夏休みを日本で過ごしたいです。 = I want to spend my summer vacation in Japan.
- 毎日を大切に過ごします。 = I make the most of every day

mnemonic: It is composed of 単 (single) and 語 (language). Think of it as 'a single piece of language'. For 'a vocabulary list', say 単語帳 (たんごちょう).
examples: - 新しい単語を覚えます。 = I memorize new words.
- この単語の意味は何ですか。 = What does this word mean?
- 毎日、単語を十個勉強します。 = I study ten words every day.
- 単語帳を買いました。 = I bought a vocabulary notebook.

mnemonic: It is composed of 表 (express/surface) and 現 (appear). Think of it as 'making something appear on the surface'. Add する to get the verb 表現する, 'to express'.
examples: - 便利な表現を教えてください。 = Please teach me a useful expression.
- この表現は丁寧です。 = This expression is polite.
- 日本語の表現は難しいです。 = Japanese expressions are difficult.
- 自分の気持ちを表現します。 = I express my own feelings.

mnemonic: It is composed of 発 (emit/start) and 音 (sound). Think of it as 'sending out a sound'. Same kanji as the Korean 발음 (bareum).
examples: - 発音が上手ですね。 = Your pronunciation is good.
- 日本語の発音は難しいですか。 = Is Japanese pronunciation difficult?
- 先生に発音を直してもらいました。 = My teacher corrected my pronunciation.
- この言葉の発音を教えてください。 = Please tell me how to pronounce this word.

mnemonic: It is composed of 歹 (bones/decay) and 匕 (person). Because 死 and 四 (four) are both read し, the number 4 is considered unlucky in Japan (as in Korea), and 4 is often read よん to avoid it. The verb is 死ぬ (しぬ), 'to die'.
examples: - 死は誰にでも来ます。 = Death comes to everyone.
- 祖父の死を悲しみました。 = I mourned my grandfather's death.
- 死を恐れる人は多いです。 = Many people fear death.
- 犬の死で、家族は泣きました。 = The family cried over the dog's death.

mnemonic: It is composed of 病 (sickness) and 気 (spirit/energy). Think of it as 'when your energy is sick'. Note that 気 appears in many expressions, such as 元気 (healthy) and 天気 (weather).
examples: - 病気で学校を休みました。 = I was absent from school because of illness.
- 姉は重い病気です。 = My older sister has a serious illness.
- 病気になる前に、運動しましょう。 = Let's exercise before we get sick.
- 早く病気が治るといいですね。 = I hope you get over your illness soon.

mnemonic: It is composed of 禁 (prohibit) and 忌 (avoid/mourning). Same kanji as the Korean 금기 (geumgi). In everyday speech, the loanword タブー is also very common.
examples: - 日本では、箸をご飯に立てるのは禁忌です。 = In Japan, sticking chopsticks upright in rice is taboo.
- 死についての話は禁忌とされています。 = Talking about death is considered taboo.
- この薬は妊娠中の人には禁忌です。 = This medicine is contraindicated for pregnant people.
- 文化によって禁忌は違います。 = Taboos differ by culture.

mnemonic: It is composed of 亻 (person) and 列 (line). Think of it as 'people lined up as examples'. You can find it in 例えば (たとえば), meaning 'for example'.
examples: - 例を挙げてください。 = Please give an example.
- 例えば、りんごやみかんです。 = For example, apples and mandarin oranges.
- この文の例を見てください。 = Please look at an example of this sentence.
- 例のとおりに書いてください。 = Please write it as in the example.

mnemonic: It is composed of 数 (count) and 字 (character). Think of it as 'counting characters'. Don't confuse 数字 (the written digit) with 数 (かず), 'the amount'.
examples: - 電話番号の数字を間違えました。 = I got a digit in the phone number wrong.
- 漢数字は読むのが難しいです。 = Kanji numerals are hard to read.
- 黒板に数字を書きます。 = I write numbers on the blackboard.
- 彼は数字に強いです。 = He is good with numbers.

mnemonic: It is composed of 一 (one) and 部 (section). Think of it as 'one section' of a whole. Its opposite is 全部 (ぜんぶ), 'all, the whole'.
examples: - 一部の人は反対しました。 = Some people objected.
- この本の一部を読みました。 = I read part of this book.
- 一部だけ変更します。 = I will change only a part.
- 機械の一部が壊れています。 = A part of the machine is broken.

mnemonic: It is composed of 建 (build) and 物 (thing). Think of it as 'a built thing'. It comes from the verb 建てる (たてる), 'to build'.
examples: - あの建物は図書館です。 = That building is a library.
- 古い建物が多い町です。 = It is a town with many old buildings.
- 建物の中に入りましょう。 = Let's go inside the building.
- 駅の隣に大きな建物があります。 = There is a large building next to the station.

tr: （アルファベット・エフ）- Alphabet letter F
mnemonic: アルファベット is a katakana loanword for 'alphabet'. Latin letters are read with their English names, so F is read エフ. Don't confuse it with ローマ字 (ローマじ), the Japanese written in Latin letters.
examples: - Fはアルファベットの六番目の文字です。 = F is the sixth letter of the alphabet.
- アルファベットを全部言えますか。 = Can you say the whole alphabet?
- 私の名前の最初はFです。 = My name starts with F.
- これはアルファベットのFです。 = This is the letter F of the alphabet.

mnemonic: It is composed of 漢 (Han/Chinese) and 字 (character). It is the Japanese equivalent of the Korean 한자 (hanja), 'Chinese characters'.
examples: - 漢字を勉強しています。 = I am studying kanji.
- この漢字の読み方がわかりません。 = I don't know how to read this kanji.
- 日本語には漢字が多いです。 = Japanese has many kanji.
- 漢字は中国から来ました。 = Kanji came from China.

mnemonic: It is composed of 類 (kind), 似 (resemble) and 性 (nature). Think of it as 'the nature of resembling'. The verb is 似ている (にている), 'to resemble'.
examples: - 二つの言語には類似性があります。 = There is a similarity between the two languages.
- 日本語と韓国語の類似性に驚きました。 = I was surprised by the similarity between Japanese and Korean.
- 文法の類似性が学習を助けます。 = Grammatical similarity helps learning.
- 二つの事件の類似性を調べます。 = I will investigate the similarity between the two incidents.

mnemonic: It is composed of 囗 (border) and 玉 (jewel). Think of it as 'a jewel inside borders'. Be careful! 国 is read こく or ごく in compounds, such as: 韓国 (かんこく) meaning 'South Korea'.
examples: - どこの国から来ましたか。 = Which country are you from?
- 日本は小さい国です。 = Japan is a small country.
- 私の国は暑いです。 = My country is hot.
- 世界にはたくさんの国があります。 = There are many countries in the world.

mnemonic: It is composed of 計 (measure) and 画 (draw/plan). Think of it as 'measuring and drawing out' what you will do. Don't confuse 計画 (a plan) with 予定 (よてい), 'a schedule'.
examples: - 旅行の計画を立てます。 = I make travel plans.
- 計画どおりに進んでいます。 = It is proceeding as planned.
- 新しい計画を説明します。 = I will explain the new plan.
- 夏休みの計画はありますか。 = Do you have plans for summer vacation?

mnemonic: It is composed of 自 (self) and 身 (body). Don't confuse 自身 (oneself) with 自信 (じしん), 'confidence'. They sound the same! The Korean 자신 covers both meanings.
examples: - 自分自身を信じてください。 = Believe in yourself.
- 私自身が行きます。 = I myself will go.
- 彼自身も知りませんでした。 = Even he himself didn't know.
- 私自身、そう思います。 = I myself think so.

mnemonic: It is composed of 注 (pour) and 意 (mind). Think of it as 'pouring your mind into something'. Add する to get the verb 注意する, 'to be careful' or 'to warn'.
examples: - 足元に注意してください。 = Please watch your step.
- 先生に注意されました。 = I was warned by my teacher.
- 車に注意しましょう。 = Let's be careful of cars.
- 注意が必要です。 = Caution is necessary.

mnemonic: It is composed of 文 (writing/literature) and 化 (change). Think of it as 'what writing and change build over time'. Same kanji as the Korean 문화 (munhwa).
examples: - 日本の文化に興味があります。 = I am interested in Japanese culture.
- 食文化は国によって違います。 = Food culture differs by country.
- 文化の違いを学びます。 = I learn about cultural differences.
- 韓国の文化が好きです。 = I like Korean culture.

mnemonic: Think of 面 as a 'face' of something: a side, a surface or an aspect. Don't confuse 面 with 麺 (めん), 'noodles', which sounds the same. 面 is also read おもて in 表面 and 面白い (おもしろい), 'interesting'.
examples: - いい面と悪い面があります。 = There are good sides and bad sides.
- この面を上にしてください。 = Please put this side up.
- 別の面から考えましょう。 = Let's think from another aspect.
- 生活の面で助かります。 = It helps in terms of daily life.

mnemonic: The four dots at the bottom (灬) can remind you of 'dots' or 'points'. You can find it in 点数 (てんすう), 'score', and 〜点 as the counter for points and marks.
examples: - 試験で百点を取りました。 = I got 100 points on the exam.
- 良い点と悪い点を考えます。 = I consider the good points and the bad points.
- この点が大切です。 = This point is important.
- 点を線でつなぎます。 = I connect the dots with lines.

mnemonic: Think of the sun rising among the grass at dawn. Be careful! 朝 is read ちょう in compounds, such as: 朝食 (ちょうしょく) meaning 'breakfast'. In casual speech, 朝ごはん is also common.
examples: - 毎朝六時に起きます。 = I wake up at six every morning.
- 朝ごはんを食べましたか。 = Did you eat breakfast?
- 今朝は寒かったです。 = It was cold this morning.
- 朝は忙しいです。 = Mornings are busy.

mnemonic: It is a katakana loanword (from Dutch 'koffie'). Remember the long vowel mark ー! The kanji 珈琲 also exists, but it is rarely used outside of cafe signs and menus.
examples: - 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。 = I drink coffee every morning.
- コーヒーに砂糖を入れますか。 = Do you put sugar in your coffee?
- 熱いコーヒーをください。 = A hot coffee, please.
- コーヒーより紅茶が好きです。 = I like tea more than coffee.

mnemonic: It is composed of 韓 (Korea) and 国 (country). Don't confuse 韓国 (Korea) with 中国 (ちゅうごく), 'China'. The language is 韓国語 (かんこくご) and a Korean person is 韓国人 (かんこくじん).
examples: - 韓国に行きたいです。 = I want to go to Korea.
- 韓国語を勉強しています。 = I am studying Korean.
- 韓国料理が大好きです。 = I love Korean food.
- 友達は韓国人です。 = My friend is Korean.

mnemonic: It is a katakana loanword (from French 'café'). The small ェ makes the 'fe' sound. The traditional Japanese-style coffee shop is called 喫茶店 (きっさてん).
examples: - カフェで友達に会います。 = I meet my friend at a cafe.
- このカフェは静かです。 = This cafe is quiet.
- カフェで勉強するのが好きです。 = I like studying at cafes.
- 駅の近くにカフェがあります。 = There is a cafe near the station.

mnemonic: It is composed of 友 (friend) and 達 (plural/reach). Think of it as 'a group of friends'. 友達 is casual, while 友人 (ゆうじん) is more formal.
examples: - 友達と映画を見ます。 = I watch a movie with my friend.
- 彼は私の大切な友達です。 = He is my important friend.
- 友達がたくさんいます。 = I have many friends.
- 友達に電話します。 = I call my friend.

mnemonic: It is composed of 週 (week) and 末 (end). Think of it as 'the end of the week'. Same kanji as the Korean 주말 (jumal).
examples: - 週末は何をしますか。 = What do you do on the weekend?
- 週末に友達と出かけます。 = I go out with friends on the weekend.
- 先週末は家にいました。 = I stayed home last weekend.
- 週末が待ち遠しいです。 = I can't wait for the weekend.

mnemonic: It is composed of 言 (speech) and 舌 (tongue). Think of it as 'speech with the tongue'. Don't confuse 話す (to talk, to speak) with 言う (いう), 'to say'.
examples: - 日本語で話してください。 = Please speak in Japanese.
- 友達と電話で話します。 = I talk with my friend on the phone.
- 先生に話したいことがあります。 = There is something I want to tell the teacher.
- 彼は英語を話せます。 = He can speak English.

mnemonic: It is composed of 避 (avoid) and ける (the hiragana ending). You can find 避 in 避難 (ひなん), meaning 'evacuation'. It is a ru-verb: 避けます, 避けない.
examples: - 混んでいる時間を避けます。 = I avoid crowded times.
- 雨を避けて、店に入りました。 = I took shelter from the rain and went into a store.
- 危ない道は避けてください。 = Please avoid dangerous roads.
- 彼は私を避けているようです。 = He seems to be avoiding me.

tr: （おもいだす）- To recall, to remember
mnemonic: It is composed of 思い (thought) and 出す (take out). Think of it as 'taking a thought out'. If you want 'to picture something in your mind', use 思い浮かべる (おもいうかべる).
examples: - この歌を聞くと、昔を思い出します。 = When I hear this song, I recall the old days.
- 彼の名前を思い出せません。 = I can't remember his name.
- 子どものころを思い出します。 = I recall my childhood.
- 宿題を思い出しました。 = I remembered the homework.

mnemonic: Think of 作 as a person (亻) doing something quickly (乍): making. Be careful! 作 is read さく or さ in compounds, such as: 作文 (さくぶん) meaning 'composition'. For big things (ships, buildings), 造る is also used.
examples: - 母は毎日料理を作ります。 = My mother makes meals every day.
- 友達とケーキを作りました。 = I made a cake with a friend.
- 新しい会社を作りたいです。 = I want to create a new company.
- 紙で箱を作ります。 = I make a box out of paper.

mnemonic: Think of 使 as 'a person (亻) at work (吏)': using something. 使う is the everyday word, while 使用する (しようする) is the formal one, and it is the exact match for the Korean 사용하다.
examples: - 箸を使って食べます。 = I eat using chopsticks.
- このペンを使ってもいいですか。 = May I use this pen?
- 毎日スマホを使います。 = I use my smartphone every day.
- 時間を上手に使ってください。 = Please use your time wisely.

tr: （いみする）- To mean, to signify
mnemonic: It is composed of 意味 (meaning) and する (to do). 意 is 'mind/intention' and 味 is 'taste', so think of it as 'the taste of an intention'. Same kanji as the Korean 의미하다 (uimihada).
examples: - この言葉は何を意味しますか。 = What does this word mean?
- 赤は「危険」を意味します。 = Red means 'danger'.
- 「ありがとう」は感謝を意味します。 = 'Arigatou' signifies gratitude.
- 沈黙は同意を意味しません。 = Silence does not mean agreement.

tr: （みなす）- To regard as, to consider as
mnemonic: It is composed of 見 (see) and なす (to make). Think of it as 'to see something as something else', and it is used with と: AをBと見なす. A softer, everyday alternative is 〜と思う (to think that).
examples: - 彼を友達と見なしています。 = I regard him as a friend.
- 沈黙は同意と見なされます。 = Silence is regarded as agreement.
- これは失礼と見なされます。 = This is regarded as rude.
- これを大切な経験と見なします。 = I regard this as a valuable experience.

mnemonic: It is composed of 訪 (visit) and 問 (ask). Think of it as 'going to ask'. It is formal. For casual visits, use 遊びに行く (あそびにいく), and for places, 訪れる (おとずれる) is also common.
examples: - 先生の家を訪問しました。 = I visited the teacher's house.
- 来週、取引先を訪問します。 = Next week, I will visit a client.
- 京都を訪問したいです。 = I want to visit Kyoto.
- 訪問する前に電話します。 = I call before visiting.

tr: （かたむける）- To tilt, to lean, to devote (attention)
mnemonic: It is composed of 傾 (lean) and ける. Like the Korean 기울이다, it is used in the expression 耳を傾ける (みみをかたむける), 'to lend an ear'. Its intransitive pair is 傾く (かたむく), 'to lean'.
examples: - 先生の話に耳を傾けます。 = I listen attentively to the teacher.
- コップを少し傾けてください。 = Please tilt the glass a little.
- 頭を傾けて考えました。 = I tilted my head and thought.
- 全力を傾けて働きます。 = I work with all my strength.

mnemonic: It is composed of 理 (reason) and 解 (untie). Think of it as 'untying the reason'. Don't confuse 理解する (to understand deeply) with 分かる (わかる), 'to understand' in everyday speech.
examples: - 日本語の文法を理解しました。 = I understood Japanese grammar.
- 彼の気持ちを理解できません。 = I can't understand his feelings.
- 説明を聞いて、やっと理解しました。 = After hearing the explanation, I finally understood.
- お互いを理解することが大切です。 = Understanding each other is important.

mnemonic: It is composed of 飲 (the 食 'eat' radical, plus 欠, an open mouth). Think of it as 'eating with an open mouth'. In Japanese, 飲む is also used for taking medicine: 薬を飲む.
examples: - 水を飲んでください。 = Please drink water.
- 友達とお茶を飲みました。 = I drank tea with a friend.
- 薬を飲む時間です。 = It's time to take medicine.
- 夜はお酒を飲みません。 = I don't drink alcohol at night.

tr: （すきだ）- To like, to be fond of
mnemonic: It is composed of 女 (woman) and 子 (child). Think of it as 'a mother loving her child'. Be careful! Grammatically 好き is a na-adjective, not a verb, so the thing you like takes が, not を: 猫が好きです.
examples: - 私は猫が好きです。 = I like cats.
- 友達は音楽が好きです。 = My friend likes music.
- 日本料理が大好きです。 = I love Japanese food.
- 彼のことが好きになりました。 = I came to like him.

tr: （おおい）- To be many, to be much
mnemonic: It is composed of two 夕 (evening) stacked up. Think of it as 'many evenings piled up'. It is an i-adjective, so use が for the thing that is many: 人が多いです. Its opposite is 少ない (すくない). Before a noun, say 多くの人.
examples: - 日本には山が多いです。 = There are many mountains in Japan.
- 今日は宿題が多いです。 = There is a lot of homework today.
- 駅は人が多いです。 = The station has a lot of people.
- 去年より雨が多かったです。 = There was more rain than last year.

mnemonic: Be careful! 行く is irregular in its て-form: 行って (not 行いて). 行 is read こう or ぎょう in compounds, such as: 旅行 (りょこう) meaning 'trip' and 銀行 (ぎんこう) meaning 'bank'. Its opposite is 来る (くる).
examples: - 学校に行きます。 = I go to school.
- 明日、友達と海へ行きます。 = Tomorrow I'm going to the sea with friends.
- 韓国に行ったことがあります。 = I have been to Korea.
- 一緒に行きましょう。 = Let's go together.

mnemonic: It is composed of 直接 (directly) and 的 (-like/-ic suffix). The suffix 的 turns nouns into adjectives, like '-tic' or '-al'. Its opposite is 間接的 (かんせつてき), 'indirect'.
examples: - 直接的な言い方は失礼になることがあります。 = Direct phrasing can sometimes be rude.
- 彼は直接的に質問しました。 = He asked directly.
- 直接的な原因は雨です。 = The direct cause is the rain.
- 日本語は間接的な表現が多いです。 = Japanese often uses indirect expressions.

tr: （とくていする）- To specify, to identify, to pinpoint
mnemonic: It is composed of 特 (special) and 定 (fix/decide). Think of it as 'fixing on something special'. 特定の (とくていの) + noun means 'a specific ...'. Same kanji as the Korean 특정하다 (teukjeonghada).
examples: - 原因を特定します。 = I identify the cause.
- 犯人はまだ特定されていません。 = The culprit has not been identified yet.
- 特定の人だけが入れます。 = Only specific people can enter.
- 場所を特定するのは難しいです。 = It is difficult to pinpoint the location.

mnemonic: It is composed of 不 (not) and 吉 (good luck). Think of it as 'not lucky'. You can find 吉 in 大吉 (だいきち), the best fortune at a shrine's おみくじ. Before a noun, say 不吉な.
examples: - 黒い猫は不吉だと言われます。 = It is said that black cats are ominous.
- 四は不吉な数字です。 = Four is an unlucky number.
- 不吉な夢を見ました。 = I had an ominous dream.
- 不吉な予感がします。 = I have a bad feeling.

tr: （ちがう）- To be different, to be wrong
mnemonic: It is composed of 違 (differ) and う. Be careful! Unlike the Korean 다르다, 違う is a verb, not an adjective. It also means 'wrong': それは違います, 'That's wrong'. The noun is 違い (ちがい), 'difference'.
examples: - 私の意見は彼と違います。 = My opinion is different from his.
- 国によって文化が違います。 = Culture differs by country.
- 日本語と韓国語は少し違います。 = Japanese and Korean are a little different.
- それは違います。 = That's wrong.

mnemonic: It is composed of 不 (not) and 便 (convenient). Think of it as 'not convenient'. Its opposite is 便利 (べんり), 'convenient'. Before a noun, say 不便な.
examples: - この町は電車が少なくて不便です。 = This town is inconvenient because there are few trains.
- 家の近くに店がなくて不便です。 = There are no stores near my house, so it's inconvenient.
- 古い携帯は不便でした。 = The old mobile phone was inconvenient.
- 不便な生活に慣れました。 = I got used to an inconvenient life.

tr: （こうだ）- To be like this, to be so
mnemonic: It belongs to the こそあど family: こう (like this), そう (like that), ああ (like that, far away), どう (how). Alternatives with the same meaning are このようだ and こんなふうだ.
examples: - 結果はこうです。 = The result is like this.
- こうすれば簡単です。 = It's easy if you do it like this.
- 問題はこうなっています。 = The problem stands like this.
- こうしてはいられません。 = I can't stay like this.

mnemonic: It is composed of 言語 (language) and 的 (-ic suffix). Think of it as 'language-related'. Its opposite is 非言語的 (ひげんごてき), 'non-verbal'.
examples: - 言語的な違いが大きいです。 = The linguistic differences are large.
- 言語的な能力が高い子どもです。 = He is a child with high linguistic ability.
- 非言語的なコミュニケーションも大切です。 = Non-verbal communication is also important.
- これは言語的な問題ではありません。 = This is not a linguistic problem.

mnemonic: It is composed of 興味 (interest) and 深い (deep). Think of it as 'deeply interesting'. 興味がある means 'to be interested', and the casual word for 'interesting/funny' is 面白い (おもしろい).
examples: - この話はとても興味深いです。 = This story is very interesting.
- 興味深い本を読みました。 = I read an interesting book.
- 彼の研究は興味深いです。 = His research is intriguing.
- 日本の歴史は興味深いと思います。 = I think Japanese history is fascinating.
